question: What best describes hospital policies?

options.A: Rules made exclusively by individual nurses for their patients
options.B: Overarching rules and standards established by management to govern institutional operations and care
options.C: Temporary suggestions that staff can choose to follow or ignore
options.D: Laws enacted by the national legislature regarding medical licensing

explanation: Hospital policies are overarching rules, regulations, and standards set by hospital management to govern institutional operations and patient care standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h1)

question: How do departmental policies differ from hospital-wide policies?

options.A: They are completely unrelated to hospital administration
options.B: They focus only on financial budgeting
options.C: They narrow down broad directives to fit the specialized needs of specific units

explanation: Departmental policies take broad hospital directives and narrow them down to address the specialized needs and clinical requirements of specific hospital units. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which regulatory body in Nigeria oversees professional nursing standards that align with institutional practices?

options.B: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) is the primary regulatory body overseeing professional nursing practice and standards in the country. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h2)

question: What is a potential legal consequence for a nurse who unjustifiably deviates from established hospital policies resulting in patient harm?

options.C: Evidence of a breach of the standard of care leading to potential liability

explanation: Unjustifiable deviation from established policies resulting in harm serves as evidence of a breach of the standard of care, potentially resulting in legal liability or disciplinary action. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which level sits at the top of the healthcare policy and regulatory framework hierarchy?

options.B: National acts, legislative decrees, and health ministry guidelines

explanation: National acts, legislative decrees, and health ministry guidelines sit at the top of the healthcare policy hierarchy, establishing the legal boundaries for healthcare delivery. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why must a nurse understand the hierarchy of healthcare policies?

options.A: To ensure lower-level protocols do not conflict with higher-level legal and professional mandates
options.B: So they can rewrite national laws at their convenience
options.C: To avoid ever having to document patient care
options.D: Because it determines their monthly salary

explanation: Understanding the hierarchy ensures nurses know that institutional and departmental protocols must always remain consistent with higher-level legal and professional mandates. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a hospital-wide policy?

options.B: Universal hand hygiene and infection control mandates
options.C: Specific blood transfusion concentration for pediatric oncology
options.D: Emergency surgical tray setup for orthopedics

explanation: Universal hand hygiene and infection control mandates apply to all staff and departments across the entire facility, making them hospital-wide policies. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h4)

question: What characterizes a departmental protocol compared to a hospital-wide policy?

options.A: It applies universally to every single hospital employee without exception
options.B: It is tailored to the unique clinical workflows and specialized equipment of a specific unit
options.C: It is created by national legislators

explanation: Departmental protocols are specifically tailored to address the unique clinical workflows, specialized equipment, and specialized needs of a particular unit. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h4)

question: What typically triggers the initiation of a new policy or a policy revision?

options.A: A desire to make paperwork more complicated
options.B: A recognized need stemming from adverse events, new research, or updated regulations
options.D: Individual staff preferences on uniform colors

explanation: Policy development is triggered by recognized needs such as clinical adverse events, new research findings, or updated legislative requirements. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why do established hospital policies require a scheduled review lifecycle (e.g., every two to three years)?

options.A: To ensure they remain clinically accurate, relevant, and evidence-based
options.B: To ensure they are permanently forgotten
options.C: Because hospital management has too much free time
options.D: To change the font size of the documents

explanation: Scheduled reviews ensure that policies keep pace with current evidence-based practice, technological changes, and evolving regulatory standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why are nurses considered to have a frontline role in policy implementation?

options.A: They write all national healthcare laws
options.B: They form the largest workforce segment providing continuous bedside care and translating rules into action
options.C: They are exempt from following hospital rules
options.D: They manage the hospital financial budget

explanation: Nurses comprise the largest segment of healthcare workers and provide round-the-clock bedside care, making them critical for translating written policies into daily clinical practice. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is a key outcome when nurses consistently comply with evidence-based hospital policies?

options.B: Protection of patients from harm and fostering of interprofessional trust
options.C: Elimination of the need for patient documentation
options.D: Extended hospital stays for all patients

explanation: Consistent policy compliance protects patients from preventable medical errors, builds interprofessional trust, and upholds professional standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h6)

question: What should a nurse do when they identify an outdated or impractical policy in their clinical unit?

options.A: Quietly ignore the policy forever without telling anyone
options.B: Report the gap or discrepancy through proper institutional channels for review
options.C: Complain publicly on social media about the hospital
options.D: Write a new national law independently

explanation: Nurses have a professional duty to report policy gaps and deviations through proper institutional channels like incident reporting systems or unit managers for constructive review. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h7)

question: How does identifying and reporting policy gaps benefit the healthcare institution?

options.A: It contributes to continuous quality improvement and institutional learning
options.B: It increases the rate of clinical errors
options.C: It reduces the need for nursing documentation

explanation: Reporting gaps serves as a constructive mechanism for continuous quality improvement, helping management refine and update policies. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h7)

question: What is a primary effect of standardized hospital policies on clinical practice?

options.B: They reduce unwarranted clinical variation and help prevent medical errors
options.D: They make clinical outcomes impossible to measure

explanation: Standardized policies minimize unwarranted clinical variation, which directly helps prevent medical errors and adverse events. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h8)

question: How do policies assist hospitals in tracking and improving quality of care?

options.A: They provide measurable evidence-based benchmarks against which clinical outcomes and safety indicators are evaluated
options.B: They hide adverse events from the nursing staff
options.C: They replace the need for clinical audits
options.D: They eliminate all forms of patient assessment

explanation: Policies establish evidence-based benchmarks that serve as measurable standards for clinical audits, outcome evaluations, and safety indicator tracking. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h8)
